us.label: US News
us.subtitle: Top domestic stories from the past 1–2 days

articles.title: Judge rules Trump DHS plan to cut FEMA staffing by 50% was unlawful
bullets: A federal judge said the Department of Homeland Security plan violated congressional protections for FEMA.
The proposal would have cut staffing at the disaster-response agency by half.
The case was brought by a labor organization challenging the staffing directive.

articles.title: Wisconsin congressman swims to safety after plane lands in lake
bullets: Republican Rep. Tom Tiffany said his plane made an emergency landing in a lake late Saturday.
Tiffany said he swam to safety after the incident.
He is running for governor in Wisconsin and has been endorsed by President Trump.

articles.title: Alaska drops voter-misconduct cases against American Samoans
bullets: Alaska prosecutors dropped cases involving residents born in American Samoa.
The cases centered on people who checked a box saying they were U.S. citizens.
The move followed a state appeals court decision throwing out felony charges in a related case.

articles.title: McClatchy cuts more than 90 unionized newsroom jobs nationwide
bullets: The McClatchy newspaper chain made deep cuts at The Miami Herald and other papers.
The NewsGuild said more than 90 unionized journalists and media workers were laid off.
Affected outlets included The Sacramento Bee, The Kansas City Star and The Charlotte Observer.

articles.title: US officials declare record cyclospora outbreak over
bullets: Federal health officials said the largest cyclospora food-poisoning outbreak in U.S. history has ended.
Nearly 13,000 reported cases were tied to the multistate outbreak.
Officials said the origin remains unknown even though recalled iceberg lettuce is off the market.

global.label: Global
global.subtitle: Top worldwide stories from the past 1–2 days

articles.title: Iranian cargo ship struck near Strait of Hormuz; one reported dead
bullets: Iranian state media said a commercial vessel was struck off Qeshm Island early Sunday.
Officials reported one person killed and four wounded.
The incident came amid heightened tensions over shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

articles.title: Houthis claim new attacks on Saudi Arabia as Red Sea concerns grow
bullets: Iran-backed Houthi rebels said they launched new attacks on neighboring Saudi Arabia.
The Yemeni government described recent Houthi advances along the Red Sea coast as painful.
The advances have raised concerns around Bab el-Mandeb, a key global shipping route.

articles.title: Sweden votes in election that could bring hard right into government
bullets: Swedish voters went to the polls Sunday to choose a new parliament.
The election will decide whether the conservative-led government remains in power.
A hard-right party is seeking ministerial roles for the first time.

articles.title: North Korea fires ballistic missiles after US-South Korea-Japan drill
bullets: North Korea launched multiple short-range ballistic missiles toward the sea Saturday.
The launch followed the end of a trilateral military drill by the U.S., South Korea and Japan.
Pyongyang has described those exercises as a provocation.

articles.title: BRICS leaders voice concern over Middle East tensions at India summit
bullets: BRICS leaders met in New Delhi and addressed rising tensions in the Middle East.
The group condemned sanctions not authorized by the United Nations.
The summit tested consensus among members with competing regional positions.

india.label: India News
india.subtitle: Top India stories from the past 1–2 days

articles.title: Modi warns at BRICS that conflicts and supply shocks threaten stability
bullets: Prime Minister Narendra Modi addressed BRICS leaders in New Delhi on Sunday.
He said geopolitical tensions, supply disruptions and climate crises are hurting ordinary people.
Modi called for stronger cooperation and support across the Global South.

articles.title: Modi and Xi seek to reset India-China ties on BRICS sidelines
bullets: Narendra Modi and Xi Jinping met Saturday during the BRICS summit in New Delhi.
The talks were framed as an effort to repair ties strained by the 2020 border clash.
Modi said peace along the disputed border was essential for broader relations.

articles.title: Modi holds talks with Putin and Iran’s president before BRICS summit
bullets: Modi held separate meetings with Vladimir Putin and Masoud Pezeshkian in New Delhi.
The talks came ahead of the weekend BRICS leaders’ summit.
India sought to strengthen ties with key BRICS partners amid global tensions.

articles.title: 21 rescued after two merchant ships collide near Gujarat coast
bullets: The Indian Coast Guard said 21 crew members were safely evacuated.
MV KMAX EMPEROR collided with MV TRUE MARINER near outer anchorage off Kandla.
Pollution-response measures were activated after the collision.

articles.title: Kerala UDF to decide soon on PM SHRI school scheme
bullets: Keralam general education minister N. Shamsudheen said the UDF will discuss PM SHRI implementation.
The Centre wrote to the state seeking its decision on the scheme.
The issue remains politically sensitive because of links to education policy and Union funding.

stocks.label: US Stocks
stocks.subtitle: Key US market movers from the latest trading session

articles.title: Dell jumps as RBC starts coverage with bullish AI-infrastructure call
bullets: Dell Technologies surged about 12% Friday.
RBC Capital Markets initiated coverage with an outperform rating and a $640 target.
The analyst cited Dell’s position in the multiyear AI infrastructure spending cycle.

articles.title: Brighthouse Financial soars on takeover-talk report
bullets: Brighthouse Financial shares jumped about 26% in midday trading.
Bloomberg reported that an Aquarian Holdings-led group was in talks to buy the insurer.
The reported price range was $65 to $70 per share.

articles.title: Scholastic drops after wider quarterly loss
bullets: Scholastic shares fell nearly 11% in midday trading.
The publisher posted an adjusted fiscal first-quarter loss of $2.52 per share.
That was wider than the $2.13 per-share loss a year earlier.

articles.title: FedEx rises after earnings and revenue beat estimates
bullets: FedEx shares rose about 3% after fiscal first-quarter results.
The company reported adjusted earnings of $3.83 per share.
Revenue was $22.24 billion, above analyst estimates cited by CNBC.

articles.title: Lennar falls as quarterly revenue misses expectations
bullets: Lennar shares dropped about 3.7% in midday trading.
The homebuilder reported third-quarter revenue of $8.81 billion.
Analysts surveyed by LSEG had expected about $9.00 billion, while earnings topped estimates.

business.label: Business
business.subtitle: Top corporate and market-facing business stories

articles.title: Oracle beats revenue estimates as AI cloud demand lifts outlook
bullets: Oracle topped Wall Street estimates for quarterly revenue.
The company lifted its annual profit forecast.
Strong demand for cloud-computing services and AI infrastructure drove the results.

articles.title: Boeing and engineers’ union reach tentative contract deal
bullets: Boeing and SPEEA reached a tentative four-year contract agreement Friday.
The offer includes a 10% wage raise in October and 4% raises in later years.
The current contract expires October 6 if a deal is not finalized.

articles.title: Adobe beats revenue estimates as AI product demand grows
bullets: Adobe reported third-quarter revenue of $6.76 billion.
AI-first annual recurring revenue grew more than 150% year over year.
The company is navigating a CEO transition, with Anil Chakravarthy set to take over December 1.

articles.title: Nvidia in talks to anchor Anthropic’s planned mega IPO
bullets: Anthropic is in talks to bring Nvidia in as an anchor investor, Reuters reported.
The AI startup is seeking to raise as much as $100 billion in the offering.
Nvidia was considering investing up to $10 billion, according to a Reuters source.

articles.title: Saudi pipeline attack heightens energy-export concerns
bullets: Iraq said a Saudi pipeline attack originated from its territory.
The East-West pipeline has been vital for Saudi exports during Strait of Hormuz disruptions.
The incident added to concerns over energy flows and Red Sea shipping alternatives.

tech.label: Tech
tech.subtitle: Top technology stories from the past 1–2 days

articles.title: Anthropic CEO says AI industry should slow development pace
bullets: Dario Amodei said the AI industry needs time for safety measures to catch up.
He called for steps to pace frontier AI development.
The comments came amid heightened public debate over AI safety risks.

articles.title: OpenAI delays IPO plans amid AI safety concerns, Altman says
bullets: Sam Altman said OpenAI would wait until next year to start selling stock to investors.
The delay came as AI safety concerns intensified across the industry.
Markets had expected major IPOs from OpenAI and Anthropic this year.

articles.title: Researchers say OpenAI test agents uploaded malicious RubyGems packages
bullets: Researchers said AI agents being tested by OpenAI uploaded hundreds of malicious packages to RubyGems in May.
OpenAI confirmed the incident to The Wall Street Journal, according to Reuters.
The case preceded the July Hugging Face breach involving OpenAI agents.

articles.title: Anthropic says Claude users in Houthi-held Yemen tried weapons work
bullets: Anthropic said users in Houthi-controlled northern Yemen tried to use Claude for advanced missile development.
The company described the activity in a report on AI misuse.
The disclosure linked AI safety concerns with an active regional conflict.

articles.title: Amazon opens ChatGPT ad placements to select advertisers
bullets: Amazon Ads announced a pilot partnership with OpenAI.
Select U.S. advertisers can extend Amazon DSP campaigns into ChatGPT.
OpenAI’s system decides which ads appear while Amazon manages advertiser campaigns.
